target_customer: Institutional investors (pension funds, asset managers), public companies and governance advisors who vote proxies and manage stewardship
problem: Institutions vote thousands of shareholder meetings and rely on proxy advisors or manual research. They want to apply their own voting policies at scale with source-linked evidence and audit trails.
business_model: B2B SaaS for stewardship and proxy voting workflows (pricing not public)
product_category: AI proxy voting and corporate governance intelligence

founders.name: Ryan Nowicki Stewart
founders.background_notes: YC page: 10+ years in asset management, proxy voting and shareholder activism; Palantir Startup Fellowship cohort 002.

founders.name: Tomas Taylor
previous_startups: Mindware, agent tooling infrastructure (outcome not stated)
founders.background_notes: YC page: co-founded ClawCon; met Ryan as Cornell undergraduates.

competitors.name: ISS
competitors.what: Incumbent proxy advisor adding AI enabled voting recommendation tools
competitors.traction_then: with Glass Lewis holds over 90% of the proxy advice market per sources

competitors.name: JPMorgan Asset Management Proxy IQ
competitors.what: In-house AI voting tool replacing ISS and Glass Lewis from the 2026 proxy season
competitors.traction_then: internal use at a large asset manager

technical_complexity.rationale: Requires grounded extraction from filings and meeting materials and applying client policy rules with human review. Standard LLM engineering with a verification and audit burden.

defensibility.rationale: Client policies, decision history and audit trails create switching costs. Incumbents and in-house tools at large managers are credible alternatives.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: As of 2026 ISS announced AI features and JPMorgan built its own tool; no move aimed at Pennant specifically was found.

market_need_then: A December 2025 executive order and reported FTC scrutiny targeted ISS and Glass Lewis, and JPMorgan dropped them for in-house AI in 2026, creating demand for policy-driven voting tools.

branding.domain_note: Uses getpennant.ai, a prefix plus .ai domain.

identity.voice_and_tone: credible, finance professional, world model positioning

branding.brand_signature: Playful product names ProxyGuessr, Proposal Pilot and Governance Arena
branding.community_and_virality: Founder appeared on The Deal podcast Activist Investing Today and was featured in Harvard Law School Forum on Corporate Governance coverage; early press covers the seed round.

brand_strength.rationale: Early press exists for the raise and founder, but name is shared with an unrelated lending company called Pennant Technologies, which can confuse search.

outcome_analysis: Pennant is an active Summer 2026 company that announced a $5M seed in October 2026 led by Urban Innovation Fund. Former institutional proxy voters as founders, plus regulatory pressure on ISS and Glass Lewis and large managers moving in house, created timing. The risk is that incumbents and in-house tools absorb the wedge, and later outcomes are unknown.
notes: The $5M seed is confirmed by a law firm press release and trade press (fintech.global, citybiz, runtimewire). Dealroom lists a conflicting $125K seed entry, treated as an outlier. Lead investor Urban Innovation Fund comes from press coverage, not the Goodwin snippet. Outcome search found no shutdown or acquisition. Tumelo page undated. Pennant Technologies (lending) is an unrelated company.
